title: Welcome to My Blog
text:
A space for sharing research and reflections.


Welcome to my blog!
This platform serves as a space for me to share reflections on my research journey, including theoretical insights, methodological explorations, and analytical code. I plan to update it periodically with content related to the topics I’m currently working on, the questions I’m grappling with, and the approaches I’m experimenting with in the field of educational and social science research. In addition to research-related content, I will also occasionally share curated reading lists and research reflections on selected academic articles.
You’ll find posts introducing conceptual frameworks, walkthroughs of data analysis in R, and brief commentaries on emerging methods in quantitative social science research. Some posts may be informal or exploratory which intended to spark dialogue rather than offer definitive answers.
All content on this blog is shared in the spirit of open academic exchange. If you notice any inaccuracies in methods, theoretical interpretations, or data approaches, I warmly welcome your comments and corrections. If you’d like to connect or discuss further, feel free to reach out via email [aishuhan@ucla.edu].
Thank you for visiting, and I hope you find something here that resonates with your own work or sparks new ideas.
Warmly,
Alice

title: Hello, nice to e-meet you!
text:
I’m Shuhan Ai, but feel free to call me Alice. I am a Ph.D. student in Higher Education and Organizational Change (HEOC) and an M.S. student in Statistics & Data Science at UCLA. I study educational research with my Ph.D. advisor, Professor Kevin Eagan, and learn advanced quantitative methods with my M.S. advisor, Professor Qing Zhou.
My research focuses on the fields of STEM education, higher education policy, and student development, especially during key transitions in the academic pipeline. I investigate: (1) how students make decisions about STEM majors and careers when transitioning from high school to college; (2) what factors influence persistence, graduation, and major-changing during undergraduate study; and (3) what drives students to pursue graduate education in STEM. Through these areas, I aim to uncover the structural and cultural factors that shape educational trajectories, with a particular interest in improving diversity and representation in STEM. As study shows, diversity fosters innovation and advancement in science and technology (Hofstra et al. 2020).
As a first-generation college student and woman of color, my life and academic experiences shape my research lens. I use asset-based frameworks such as Community Cultural Wealth to highlight the strengths students bring to their educational journeys and challenge deficit-based narratives.
Methodologically, my research draws from a range of quantitative techniques, including causal inference, multilevel modeling, structural equation modeling, survival analysis, and social network analysis. I aim to integrate my interdisciplinary background to examine social and educational systems, with a commitment to promoting social justice.
